sermon.title: Seven Churches Part 2
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “Seven Churches Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer walks through Jesus’ letters to the seven churches in Revelation 2–3, using people in the room to represent each church. He highlights what Jesus commends, corrects and promises each one, and what the letters share: “I know your works,” a call to repent, and the call to overcome.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: this was a live teaching with people in the room standing in for each church; he addresses two men by first name (Paul and Lou) and once uses “James” in an illustration. The captions garble a word before “important things” and one word in Revelation 3:5 (“white attire, [unclear]”), shown as [unclear]. He says “in Psalms it says the righteous falls seven times”; that wording is Proverbs 24:16. He pronounces “Pergamus”; the English Bible reads “Pergamos.” He says “eye salve” where the captions read “IA.” He gives his own descriptions of the Nicolaitans, Balaam and Jezebel, and strong opinions on the rapture, feminism, atheists, homosexuals, America’s history and other denominations.

chunks.section_question: Why does Jesus say “I know your works” to every church, and what does he praise in Ephesus? (Revelation 2:1-3)
chunks.short_answer: He says all seven churches hear “I know your works,” which “starts right off shattering American theology.” He says grace and works go together, and that Ephesus is praised for testing false apostles, patient labor and persevering: “you fall down, you get back up.”
chunks.text:
Here we go, first church. Ready? Now we’ll say this group over here is the church of Ephesus. This is God talking to you, and he says, every one of them, he says to the angel of the church (he’s writing this to the church leaders), “I know your works.” And honestly, church, in every church he’s going to lead out by saying, “I know your works.” In America we are so strong on “not by works, it’s by grace.” No, works is out, works is out. And yet to every church, all seven, he says, “I know your works.” So are works important? Yeah. It starts right off shattering American theology. “I know your works.” “But I’m not under works, I’m under grace.” “I know your works.” “You may be under grace, my child, but I know your lifestyle.

I know what you’re thinking. I know what you’re doing.” And he says, “You labor, and you are patient, and you cannot bear those who are evil, and you have tested those who say they’re apostles and are not, and have found them liars.” Boy, I wish the American church would do that. We’d get rid of almost all of our false ministers today if they were just tested by the Scripture. “I have...” Okay, you have persevered, you have been persistent, you keep trying. How about you? Do you keep trying? You know, you fall down, you get back up. I mean, in Psalms it says the righteous falls seven times but the Lord picks him up. I don’t have to stay down because I fall. I don’t have to stay down because I make a mistake. He says, “You keep trying.”

This church is looking good, isn’t it? Man, you get up and keep trying. You guys are looking pretty good over here. You cannot bear evil people. Man, you don’t like it when people promote evil and say it’s okay. You have tested the false prophets. You have labored and not become weary. You didn’t do like a lot of Christians: they serve God for a couple of years and then, boom, you know, they get in the church and man, they get involved and all that, then after, you know, a couple years, boom, you don’t see them anymore. Just why? They get weary. Why? Because they don’t feed themselves. You can’t give if you don’t receive. But this church is not weary. They keep trying, they are persistent. But he says, “I got a little problem with you.

chunks.section_question: What does it mean to leave your “first love”? (Revelation 2:4-5)
chunks.short_answer: He says the first commandment is to love God, and Ephesus got busy “laboring and winning souls and feeding the poor” while they “stopped doing the first part of the priesthood.” He says the fix is to “repent,” “do the first works,” and get into the Bible, prayer and worship.
chunks.text:
You have left your first love.” Now, what does that mean? Well, we know the first commandment is what? Love God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your might, with all your strength. Amen. Jesus said he wants us to love him, isn’t that right? And so they got busy laboring and winning souls and feeding the poor and visiting people in the hospital and all the rest, and what they were doing, the second part of the priesthood, and they had stopped doing the first part of the priesthood. They left their first love. They [unclear] important things so that you have something to give when you go and labor. Amen, and that’s a big thing. He says you need to repent. What’s the word? Repent. Christians need to what? Repent. Turn from the error, do the first works.

What is the first work? Love God. Get into the Bible, get into prayer, you know, get into church and worship and seek him and touch him like John did. Jesus touched him when he got spiritual, when he turned, when he fell on his face before him, Jesus touched him. Isn’t that beautiful? And if you don’t, he says your lampstand is going to be moved. Now, where’s the lampstand? You remember the picture? Where’s the lampstand? It’s where Jesus was. Jesus was in the midst of the what? Lampstand. The churches. The lampstands are the what? Churches. And in spite of this church leaving their first love, the presence of God was still there. The presence of God is not his approval. Don’t ever forget that. He wants you to keep changing into his image. Isn’t that a good amen?

chunks.section_question: Is the presence of God the same as his approval? What does removing the lampstand mean? (Revelation 2:5)
chunks.short_answer: He says “the presence of God is not his approval,” because Jesus was still among Ephesus even though they had left their first love. He says removing the lampstand means “he’s going to remove his presence,” and that without love our works are “worthless.”
chunks.text: Isn’t it comforting to know that though they had broken the top commandment, Jesus was still in their midst, but he wasn’t happy with them in this area, and he come to correct them, and he says, “If you don’t get back to your first love, I’ll take your lampstand out.” What does that mean? He’s going to remove his presence. Amen. And we need his presence. Let me tell you, helping the poor and visiting the sick and all these things that we do to be nice Christian people means nothing without him. And that’s what 1 Corinthians 13 says: without love (God is love), without God your tongues, your arms, your prophecies, your miracles and all that are worthless. Amen. Why? Because God’s got to be first. Now, you hate the Nicolaitans. The Nicolaitans, the only place we can find a source on them is from the early church fathers who wrote about them and said they were an unrestrained group that shared wives.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Remember therefore from where you have fallen; repent and do the first works, or else I will come to you quickly and remove your lampstand from its place—unless you repent.

Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing. And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, but have not love, it profits me nothing.

chunks.section_question: Who were the Nicolaitans, and what is the reward of the tree of life? (Revelation 2:6-7)
chunks.short_answer: He says the only source on the Nicolaitans is the early church fathers, who described “an unrestrained group that shared wives,” and that they liked “to be the boss.” He says God said, “I hate this kind of Christian that live unrestrained lives,” but tells even this church that “you can overcome” and eat from the tree of life.
chunks.text:
Okay, that’s all we have on them. And also they like to take [unclear] they like to be the boss. I mean, you know, a lot of Christians in America want to be the boss. They want to decide what’s right and wrong, and, you know, instead of Jesus being the boss. And they live unrestrained lives, and the Ephesians recognized that and said that’s wrong, and God said himself, “I hate this kind of Christian that live unrestrained lives.” And then he says, “He that overcomes, he will eat of the tree of life, which is in the paradise of God.” Hallelujah! So what’s the reward? The tree of life. And remember, he says to this Ephesian church, you can overcome. You can do it, man. He didn’t come and say, “You’re out.” He said, “You can overcome. You can conquer this thing.”

And he says it to every church, and it’s important that we understand that, to every church and in every problem that they had, at the end he says, “Come on, you can overcome,” and you overcome, you conquer, you get victory, and “I will give you something.” And his presence is still there, and that’s what fools us in America. The people say, “Well, the presence of God was there.” That doesn’t mean God approves what the church is doing. Amen. “But I feel his presence.” That doesn’t mean God’s approving you either. He’s just faithful. He wants us to correct those things that need to be corrected. All right.

chunks.section_question: What does Jesus tell the poor, persecuted church of Smyrna? (Revelation 2:8-11)
chunks.short_answer: He says Smyrna was “poor” yet called “rich” because “the true riches is the riches of the kingdom.” He says Jesus warns of “ten days” of tribulation, tells them to “be faithful to death,” and promises a crown of life and that they will not be hurt by the second death, which he says is the lake of fire.
chunks.text:
Now here’s the church of Smyrna right here. We only got one Smyrna church member here. Boy, they’re the angel of the church or the member of the church, they’re everything right here. All right. “I know your works, your tribulation, your poverty.” I mean, you know, some Christians are just dirt poor, and it may not be because they didn’t go to school or try to learn a job skill or whatever. They may just have been born in a place where poverty is just, you know, abundant. I mean, some nations, they are ran by a government that just keeps the people in poverty. But he says, “You’re rich.” Now, why did he say they were rich? Because the true riches is the riches of the kingdom. So don’t get down on yourself because you’re poor, but don’t stay down there if you can get up.

Jeez. Now, “you have some in your midst that say they’re Jews but are of the synagogue of Satan.” Do we have people today that say they’re Christians, but you would never know it? They act just like the people that follow Satan. Isn’t that true? And that’s what happens here. He says don’t fear the suffering that’s coming. Well, we don’t like to hear those messages, man. We want joy, hallelujah, we want money. He says, “Don’t you fear. Don’t you be afraid, because there’s a coming suffering. In fact, the Devil is going to give you tribulation for ten days. He is going to test you for ten days.” Wow, how do you feel about that, member church member? Huh? “Be faithful to death.” Oh my gosh, I may not get out of this tribulation alive. Wow. You wouldn’t do that, would you, Lord?

You wouldn’t really, you know, they’re going to kill me. Some of them, we’re going to die here. “But I will give you a crown of life if you’re faithful to death.” How many? You know, we need to be faithful to Jesus till the day we die, regardless of our poverty, our riches, or what our circumstances are in life. We are to be faithful to him, amen, and then we inherit that crown of life. And he says to he that overcomes, “You will not be hurt by the second death.” The second death is the lake of fire, as we will get to, that burns for eternity, and that’s where people go that reject Christ and his word, the lake of fire. He said you won’t be hurt by the lake of fire. And don’t you be afraid of the tribulation and troubles that come.

Church, this should be very liberating for you. Troubles are normal, and some troubles are Satan given the authority to test you like he tested Job, knowing you’re going to come out fine. See, God already knew Job could handle it. Job did not serve God because he was wealthy, had a great home and all this and people looked up to him. He served God because he loved God and he knew God, and no trouble can distract you from that. Hallelujah. Okay.

chunks.section_question: What is the “doctrine of Balaam,” and what is wrong with preachers who are in it for the money? (Revelation 2:12-15)
chunks.short_answer: He says Pergamus lived where “Satan’s throne is” yet held fast, and had the doctrine of Balaam: advising Israel into “sexual immorality” and idol offerings “for the money.” He says some preachers “just want the money” and tell people “how good you are,” and he asks why, if “give me your money and you’ll be blessed” worked, it did not work for the messenger.
chunks.text:
Then he comes to the next church, Pergamus, and he says, “I know your works. You dwell where Satan’s throne is.” Man, these people lived in the pits. How many, you know, some areas of the world are worse than others. There’s really horrible things going on, and this church was in a bad place. Yet “you hold fast to my name.” You’re faithful to my name, “and you did not deny my faith when Antipas was martyred,” one of them was killed, and they didn’t give in. “You dwell where Satan dwells.” Some have the doctrine of Balaam. You’re doing great in these areas, but you got the doctrine of Balaam. The doctrine of Balaam is: he advised Israel to commit sexual immorality and offer things sacrificed to idols, and he was in it for the money. He wanted to get payment.

How many preachers are in it for the money in America? That’s the doctrine of Balaam. You take their money away, you take their message away. Are you guys out there? And as long as you’re sending in the money, they don’t care if you’re shacking up, living with someone and committing sexual immorality or whatever. They don’t care if you got, you know, idols in your home, images and fetishes and all this stuff. They don’t care. They just want the money, and they just want to tell you how good you are. Just keep bringing the money in. “If you want to be blessed, give me your money and you’ll be blessed.” You know why? Don’t he give their money, him his money to him so he’d be blessed? You ever think of that? If this worked so good, why didn’t it work for the messenger?

Man, if this works, I just give all the money back to the people and I’m blessed. See, the truth sets you free, doesn’t it? Yes. And here’s that Nicolaitan doctrine again, and we already went through that. So they have two. This is this church over here, man, they’re all messed up. Look at them, got all kinds of weird doctrines going on. And he says to this church, “Repent, or I will war against you with my word.” “I will war against you.” Well, Jesus only does good. Yeah, yeah, sure. He also corrects, and he corrects with his word. Remember, we taught that. And he corrects with bringing opposition in your life to wake you up. You see again, young people, if God cannot be involved in the earth and correct me and punish people, he’s a worthless God.

chunks.section_question: Does God still correct and punish, and what is the “new name” on the stone? (Revelation 2:16-19)
chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus corrects “with his word” and “with bringing opposition in your life to wake you up,” and that “God is involved in the earth, and he does punish and he does judge now.” He says new names in the Bible (Abraham, Sarah, Jacob) came when God moved people “up to a different level,” and the stone’s new name means “a new job description.”
chunks.text:
What good is he? If I just live on earth and I got to experience this, when I go to heaven, what good is it doing me on earth? But the truth is, God is involved in the earth, and he does punish and he does judge now, and there’s a judgment coming. “To he that overcomes I’ll give you the hidden manna. I’ll give you a stone with a new name written on it.” And, you know, when God changed names back in the Bible, because they were moving up to a different level, isn’t that right? Abraham’s name was changed because God was moving him up to a different level. Sarah’s name was changed because God was moving him up to a different level. Jacob’s name was changed because God was moving him up to a different level.

chunks.section_question: Who is the “Jezebel” in Thyatira, and what does Jesus say he will do? (Revelation 2:20-23)
chunks.short_answer: He says Thyatira had great works but let a woman who “says she’s a prophetess” teach and lead others into “sexual immorality and worship idols.” He says “you can tell everything by the results,” that Jesus gave her time to repent, and that those who “refuse to repent” are known by their “lifestyle” and “fruit.”
chunks.text:
“You allow Jezebel to come in and teach and seduce my servants to commit sexual immorality and worship idols.” Wow. After this great stuff, they let the feminist come in. She says she’s a prophetess, and she’s not. She, she, she gave herself the title. How many, not a lot of ministers give themselves the title. And you can tell by the results. You can tell everything by the results, the fruit. He says, “I gave her time to repent.” I told her to repent. I told these people, “Do you stop it?” The people that are following her, the one that’s teaching, repent, and they wouldn’t repent. And you know that is the message to God’s church, church: that we can repent and we should repent. And how many, you know, there’s people that just refuse to repent. They justify their wrong, ain’t that right?

And you know it by their lifestyle, by their fruit. “So I’m going to put her in a sick bed of tribulation. I’m going to bring sickness, I’m going to bring tribulation on her for her works.” Her what? What’s the word? Works. Not her faith, her what? Works. “And I’m going to kill their children.” God’s going to kill innocent people, folks. You got to remember, God’s an eternal being. Death is part of the program. When he had David’s child that was conceived in sexual immorality die, he is God. Yes, that child is innocent, but that’s part of God’s program. Don’t believe this liberal thinking that, “Well, if there’s a God, why does he allow these problems in the earth?” We create the problem. Don’t blame God. The Bible says God can do no evil. See, David and Bathsheba was the one that caused this child to die, not God.

Indeed I will cast her into a sickbed, and those who commit adultery with her into great tribulation, unless they repent of their deeds. I will kill her children with death, and all the churches shall know that I am He who searches the minds and hearts. And I will give to each one of you according to your works.

chunks.section_question: Does God kill innocent people, or do we wrongly blame him? (Revelation 2:23)
chunks.short_answer: He says “death is part of the program” for an eternal God, but “we create the problem. Don’t blame God,” and “God can do no evil.” He tells atheists they cannot blame someone they say doesn’t exist, and says that when innocent people suffer it is “people” who are responsible, not God.
chunks.text:
You teenagers, you getting this? This is very important for you, because these atheists who don’t believe in God always blame God for everything on the earth, and my response to them: how can you blame someone you don’t believe in? Number one, you say he doesn’t exist, and now you’re blaming him. I says, if you really knew the book, he gave us authority, he gave us the responsibility to deal with bad things in the earth and to do right and raise our children right, and when the problems come and the payment comes, it’s our fault, not God’s. Can I hear an amen? And innocent people dying, from Genesis to Revelation, God’s people, innocent, died. Stephen died, they killed him. Prophets were stoned and killed in the Old Testament. They were innocent people. God wasn’t responsible for that death, people was.

You understand that? Please tell me you understand that. They try to turn things around and put us on the defensive. And yes, things happen to innocent people when we make bad decisions. Don’t blame God. Blame the one that made the bad decision. Could that be an amen? Now, folks, I don’t know, this is good stuff. This is the revelation of the church. You need to get this in your mind. “To the rest, the people that aren’t following Jezebel, keep what you have till I come.” Isn’t that beautiful? See, he always encourages, always encouraging. And “to they that overcome, I will give you power over the nations.” Does the church have power over the nations? And we’re diminishing. You know, we had America when I was a child (I was sharing with people yesterday) was a moral nation.

chunks.section_question: Should the church have power over the nations, and what is the “morning star”? (Revelation 2:24-28)
chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus promises “power over the nations,” and that America used to be “a moral nation” where “even bad people knew what was right and wrong.” He says we are to “overcome and get it back,” and that “the morning star” is Jesus Christ.
chunks.text:
Even bad people knew what was right and wrong. Now bad people feel they’re okay, they believe they’re okay. That’s how we’ve declined. Before the sixties, America’s impact from the religious area was very powerful. We didn’t even have supermarkets opened on Sunday. I can still remember the first time they opened up a supermarket on Sunday in Detroit, Michigan. Why? Because of the impact of the church upon the nation. And we’ve lost it in fifty years. We have lost it. But we can what? Overcome and get it back. We’re supposed to be the ones that have impact and influence over the nations. Amen. Do you get this? See, this is the revelation of the church. This is the revelation that God has for you. But they got us thinking we got to hang on to the rapture, and we got, us, you know, the church age and the, and, uh, dispensationalism.

It’s not even in the Bible. They make up this stuff and we hear it and we believe it. And this is the real dispensation, this is the real church age: we are supposed to be a force in the earth, growing into his image and becoming a, a, an element in the earth to be reckoned with. Hallelujah! And he says, “I will not only give you power over the nations, I will give you the morning star.” Who’s the morning star? Jesus Christ.

and I will give him the morning star.

chunks.section_question: What does Jesus say to Sardis, and who are “the worthy”? (Revelation 3:1-6)
chunks.short_answer: He says Sardis had “a name that you’re alive” but was dead, and was told to “strengthen the remaining things.” He says “I will come” does not mean the second coming but “coming and taking care of business,” and that “some are worthy,” including people he has met across denominations.
chunks.text:
Now here’s the church of Sardis right here. This group right here, one with the hood on his hat, and that group right there. Hallelujah! And the old man that just come from the Arctic Circle here, up there where it’s so cold, my goodness, just hearing about it I got chills running up and down my spine. But he’s so important, they can’t do without him up there. “I know your works. You are not perfect.” Well, yeah, you got me there. “You have a name that you’re alive, yeah, but you’re dead.” Woo, that’s not nice, that’s not edifying, that’s not kind, that you’re dead. You just think you’re alive. “Be watchful, be alert, strengthen the remaining things that are ready to die.” You got some good in you, you got some things in you. Come on, strengthen those things and let’s get out of this.

Amen. You see how he encourages? “Repent, and remember those things which you received and heard. Remember those things that are dying that you have. If not, if you don’t watch, I will come.” And he says “I will come” to six of the seven churches. He’s not talking about the second coming here. He’s talking about coming and taking care of business. See, we got our eyes on the second coming, we can’t see that he can come now and he can deal with us. Are you there? “Some are worthy, they’re not defiled.” Hallelujah! And you’ll find this almost everywhere you go: there are some people. I’ve been all over the world, I’ve been in every denomination, I’ve preached in almost every denomination there is in America, including the Catholic Church. And you ask around, how many Protestants have preached in a Catholic church?

But yeah, if you don’t mingle, you know, if you get this sectarian mentality where you got to be separate from everybody, how you going to impact people if you’re separated from them? And I have found that there were Catholics that loved Jesus. I was found there were Episcopalians that loved Jesus. Yeah, their church taught some weird stuff, goodness, but there were sincere, genuine, born-again people there. See, and that’s what it says here: “Some of you are worthy, you’re not defiled.” If you overcome, “I’ll give you white attire, [unclear], and I’ll put your name in the Book of Life.” Hallelujah!

Be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain, that are ready to die, for I have not found your works perfect before God.
Remember therefore how you have received and heard; hold fast and repent. Therefore if you will not watch, I will come upon you as a thief, and you will not know what hour I will come upon you.

You have a few names even in Sardis who have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy. He who overcomes shall be clothed in white garments, and I will not blot out his name from the Book of Life; but I will confess his name before My Father and before His angels.

chunks.section_question: What is the “open door” that no one can shut for Philadelphia? (Revelation 3:7-8)
chunks.short_answer: He says Philadelphia gets no rebuke and is told, “I’m going to open doors for you that nobody can shut.” He says not to worry about “the liberals … the atheists … the homosexuals and the sinners,” and that “it only takes a little strength in God” because he multiplies it.
chunks.text:
Now here’s the angel of Philadelphia here, that row in the back, nothing but women. I should have made them the Jezebel church. Huh? I wasn’t thinking good enough there. Look at him back there. Man. “I know your works. I have set before you an open door, and no man can shut it.” This is to the church of Philadelphia. He says nothing bad about this church. He said, “Because of who you are, I’m going to open doors for you that nobody can shut.” Don’t you worry about the liberals, don’t you worry about the atheists, don’t you worry about the homosexuals and the sinners. I’m going to open doors and none of these groups can shut it. Do we need that in America? Yeah, yeah. Why? Because this church was everything that he said to the other church: faithful, persistent, serving God.

“You have a little strength.” How many of you know it only takes a little strength in God? He multiplies the strength. You say, “I’m not very strong.” Well, you’re a candidate. You know, when you realize you got some strength but you’re not the total strength, then you’re a great candidate for God to do something. Now, hallelujah! When we get too confident in our strength, we eliminate ourselves, because it’s got to be him. But when we have a little strength that he is working in me, then nothing is limited. Hallelujah! How many are glad for a little strength? Amen. You know, don’t put yourself down because you feel a little strong. “You’ve obeyed my word.” Wow, did you hear that? “You’ve obeyed my word, and you have not denied my name.” “Some of them have come to you that are Jews, of Satan’s synagogue, and they lie,” and he says, “I’m going to deal with you so that they know I love you.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: “I know your works. See, I have set before you an open door, and no one can shut it; for you have a little strength, have kept My word, and have not denied My name.

chunks.section_question: What are the promises to Philadelphia: the hour of testing and the pillar in the temple? (Revelation 3:9-12)
chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus will make groups that oppose the church “know I love you,” and keep them “from the hour of testing.” He says the goal is for God to move “in us so greatly” that those groups see God’s love, and that overcomers will be “a pillar in my temple” with Jesus’s “new name.”
chunks.text:
You see, this is where the church needs to get in America, where the liberals and the atheists and the humanists, these groups that are putting down the church, and these false apostles and these false prophets and all the rest, God moves in us so greatly that those groups know God loves us. Do you see? Not that we’re some great people, but what Jesus loves us. Oh, that’s good. Maybe raise your hand and say, “I really want to see that in America.” Yeah. You see, we got to understand the promise to the church before we can get this. Promises: “I’ll keep you from the hour of testing.” Okay, that ten days of tribulation coming back there, he said it’s not going to happen to you. “I don’t need, I don’t need to fool around with this area in your life, we’re moving on.”

How many raise your hand, say, “Man, I can handle that, get out of this tribulation, we’ve had enough tribulation, we don’t need to keep having tribulation”? “The hour of testing. I come quickly. Hold fast to your crown.” See, he’s coming to do what he said he would do: open the door that no man could shut, to bring these groups that say they’re Christians and they’re not, they’re against the things of Christ, to your feet, where they know that God loves you. God’s doing it, not us. Now that’s good stuff, folks. Can he? Remember the faith of Abraham: can God perform? Does he have the power to do what he promised? See, that’s all the faith we need. We got to quit looking at our weak strength and our mistakes and our problems and start looking to him and let him come and move us up to this dominion, to this area.

Amen. “They that overcome, I’ll make him a pillar in my temple, and I’m going to give him my new name.” Not them a new name, “I’m going to give them my new name,” Jesus’s new name. You see, and there’s a sermon on that. Moses, you know, was given these new names.

He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of My God, and he shall go out no more. I will write on him the name of My God and the name of the city of My God, the New Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from My God. And I will write on him My new name.
and being fully convinced that what He had promised He was also able to perform.

chunks.section_question: What does it mean to be lukewarm, and how do we “buy” from Jesus? (Revelation 3:14-21)
chunks.short_answer: He says Laodicea says “I don’t need anything else” but is “poor, blind and naked.” He says we “buy” from Jesus by “seeking him, praying, reading his word,” not by giving money to a minister, and that even this lukewarm church “still had the presence of Jesus,” who is “always knocking.”
chunks.text:
And the last church, Paul back there all by himself, and Lou. Look at those two guys. Here we are, the Laodicean church. “I know your works. You’re neither cold nor hot. I wish that you were cold or hot, because you’re lukewarm and neither cold or hot, I’m going to vomit you out of my mouth.” Man, look at him. Hallelujah! Woo! Now, you got to remember John wrote these, wrote it seven times and sent it to the seven churches, and the seven churches are reading this, and this is the message to each church. They’re hearing what he said to the other churches, and they’re hearing what he said to us. My God, how many, you know, they can learn from all seven churches, and me, know those seven churches were written so all of us could learn.

I don’t need maturity, you know, I don’t need wisdom, I don’t need nothing, and I’m just, I’m just fine.” I meet them all the time. And God says, “You don’t know that you’re poor, blind and naked.” You can’t even see that you don’t have garments of righteousness. You can’t see anything. You don’t know anything. You’re spiritually in poverty. And then he encourages him to “buy refined gold from me, white attire, and eye salve.” Now, how do we buy from Jesus? Do we get money out of our pocket and give it to the minister? No. How do we buy? Seeking him, praying, reading his word, coming to him.

See, that’s how we purchase. We believe that his cross, his death on the cross, paid the price for everything, not just the payment for my sin, but the inheritance for my inheritance. Did they all hear what the Spirit said unto the churches?

scriptures.text_nkjv: “I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot. I could wish you were cold or hot. So then, because you are lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will vomit you out of My mouth.
Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in to him and dine with him, and he with Me.
Let your conduct be without covetousness; be content with such things as you have. For He Himself has said, “I will never leave you nor forsake you.”

chunks.section_question: What do all seven letters have in common, and what is the challenge? (Revelation 2–3)
chunks.short_answer: He says every letter says “I know your works,” every church gets “come on, we can conquer this,” and “hear what the Spirit is saying to the churches.” He says Jesus corrected six and told five to repent, that “I will come” appears six times, and that God points things out “so he can … make us better,” not to throw us out.
chunks.text:
Yeah, every church. He said, “Hear what the Spirit is saying to the churches.” He corrected six of them. Only Philadelphia did not need correction, but they were challenged to move up. Told five of them to repent. Told three of them, those of you who haven’t done these other things, you keep what you have, you maintain what you have. And so these are common. He says, “I will come” six times. “I will come, I’ll take care of business, I’ll come to make you an overcomer, I’ll come to fulfill my promises in your life.” You know, we only tell our kids things wrong in their life so that they can be straightened out. We don’t point out things in our kids wrong so we can throw them out. “Okay, I got a reason to get rid of you, James.

Out!” No. And God, he comes to point things in our life so he can what? Make us better. So get out of the guilt-trip thing and get into the conquering, overcoming mentality that you were chosen by God to become a conqueror. And he said to the angel of the seven churches to preach those things and teach those things that only Jesus allows us to teach. Could that be an amen? And we should go to churches where they teach the Bible so we can grow and become a conqueror church. This is a tremendous promise to us. This is the revelation part of it. There’s more to come. He’s not done revealing his church, but this is powerful. So you can see some weaknesses in your life and you can repent and turn from them and get up, and you can see some promises and possess them.

Hallelujah! You can be encouraged that God isn’t finished with the work that he started in you, if you’ll accept that challenge today and say, “Jesus, I’m going to spend some time like John did in spiritual things. I’m going to repent from the things that I need to repent from. If I have to do it ninety-nine times, I’m going to do it till it’s done. And Lord, I’m going to bow before you and submit to you, and I want you to touch me and empower me to possess these things.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: “He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.” ’ ”
To him who overcomes I will grant to sit with Me on My throne, as I also overcame and sat down with My Father on His throne.

faqs.question: Why does he say some Christians grow weary?
faqs.answer: He says some serve God “for a couple of years” and then you “don’t see them anymore,” because “they don’t feed themselves. You can’t give if you don’t receive.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: and you have persevered and have patience, and have labored for My name’s sake and have not become weary.

faqs.question: What does he say the Ephesians’ “first love” was?
faqs.answer: He says it is the first commandment: loving God with all your heart, soul, might and strength, so that when you “go and labor” you have something to give.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’

faqs.question: Does he say God’s presence means he approves of what a church is doing?
faqs.answer: No. He says “the presence of God is not his approval,” and that “helping the poor and visiting the sick” means “nothing without him.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Remember therefore from where you have fallen; repent and do the first works, or else I will come to you quickly and remove your lampstand from its place—unless you repent.

faqs.question: What does he say is known about the Nicolaitans?
faqs.answer: He says “the only place we can find a source on them is from the early church fathers,” who said they were “an unrestrained group that shared wives.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: But this you have, that you hate the deeds of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.

faqs.question: What does he say the second death is?
faqs.answer: He says “the second death is the lake of fire,” which “burns for eternity” for those who “reject Christ and his word,” and that overcomers “will not be hurt by the second death.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: “He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. He who overcomes shall not be hurt by the second death.” ’

faqs.question: What does he say the doctrine of Balaam looks like today?
faqs.answer: He says it is preachers who “just want the money” and “just want to tell you how good you are,” and “don’t care” about sin “as long as you’re sending in the money.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: But I have a few things against you, because you have there those who hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balak to put a stumbling block before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed to idols, and to commit sexual immorality.

faqs.question: Does he say Jesus only does good and never corrects?
faqs.answer: No. He says “he also corrects, and he corrects with his word,” and that if God “cannot be involved in the earth and correct me and punish people, he’s a worthless God.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Repent, or else I will come to you quickly and will fight against them with the sword of My mouth.

faqs.question: What does he say the Jezebel figure represents?
faqs.answer: He says it is a woman who “gave herself the title” of prophetess and leads others astray, and that you can know such people “by their lifestyle, by their fruit.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Nevertheless I have a few things against you, because you allow that woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess, to teach and seduce My servants to commit sexual immorality and eat things sacrificed to idols.

faqs.question: Does he say God kills innocent people?
faqs.answer: He says “God’s going to kill innocent people, folks,” but “God’s an eternal being,” “death is part of the program,” and “we create the problem. Don’t blame God. The Bible says God can do no evil.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: I will kill her children with death, and all the churches shall know that I am He who searches the minds and hearts. And I will give to each one of you according to your works.

faqs.question: What does he say to atheists who blame God for suffering?
faqs.answer: He says “how can you blame someone you don’t believe in? Number one, you say he doesn’t exist, and now you’re blaming him,” and that “it’s our fault, not God’s.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And they stoned Stephen as he was calling on God and saying, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.”

faqs.question: What does he say about the rapture and dispensationalism?
faqs.answer: He says “it’s not even in the Bible. They make up this stuff and we hear it and we believe it,” and that “the real church age” is that “we are supposed to be a force in the earth.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: and I will give him the morning star.

faqs.question: Does he say “I will come” in the letters is the second coming?
faqs.answer: No. He says “I will come” to six of the seven churches means “coming and taking care of business,” and that “we got our eyes on the second coming, we can’t see that he can come now and he can deal with us.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Remember therefore how you have received and heard; hold fast and repent. Therefore if you will not watch, I will come upon you as a thief, and you will not know what hour I will come upon you.

faqs.question: What does he say about believers in other denominations?
faqs.answer: He says he has preached “in almost every denomination there is in America” and found “sincere, genuine, born-again people” among Catholics and Episcopalians, and that a “sectarian mentality” keeps you from impacting people.

scriptures.text_nkjv: You have a few names even in Sardis who have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy. He who overcomes shall be clothed in white garments, and I will not blot out his name from the Book of Life; but I will confess his name before My Father and before His angels.

faqs.question: How does he say we “buy” from Jesus?
faqs.answer: He says it is not “money out of our pocket” to a minister but “seeking him, praying, reading his word, coming to him,” because “his cross, his death on the cross, paid the price for everything.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: I counsel you to buy from Me gold refined in the fire, that you may be rich; and white garments, that you may be clothed, that the shame of your nakedness may not be revealed; and anoint your eyes with eye salve, that you may see.

faqs.question: Why does he say God points out faults in our lives?
faqs.answer: He says we tell our kids what’s wrong so they can be “straightened out,” not “throw them out,” and God points things out “so he can … make us better,” so “get out of the guilt-trip thing” and into “the conquering, overcoming mentality.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: To him who overcomes I will grant to sit with Me on My throne, as I also overcame and sat down with My Father on His throne.
